SCENE 03 — Lightning ignites dry wood — final edit5.667s (7.133–12.800s)
Setting and framing: Low three-quarter medium-wide source view of a dry dead tree beneath broad storm clouds, trunk near x=52% and lower branch near x=65%, y=62%. Keep sky for the strike and readable ground depth. Both raw endpoints retain the same camera view. The controlled 100%-to-110% push belongs in editing only.
Lighting: At the start use cool diffuse storm daylight only: slate blue-gray clouds, desaturated teal distance and cool brown wood. No fire or warm firelight exists before ignition. After ignition retain the cool ambient light with only a tiny warm reflection at the burning patch.
First frame: The tree and dry lower branch are completely unlit. No lightning, flame, embers or firelight are visible. The empty woodland has no characters.
Action: Hold the unlit tree and rigid dry branch for the opening off-screen question and Arthur's Yes. At about 3.8 seconds, one fixed complete painted lightning bolt briefly joins the sky to the dry branch for a single two-frame pair, then disappears completely. It does not travel or sweep. A small flame catches at that contact after the strike. Anchor its base to that ignition point; only small upper shapes change. Keep the tree, branch and cool storm background stable. No firelight in the unlit opening and no whole-scene brightness pulse.
Edit source: clips/edit-v2/03-tight.mp4; trim source first36frames and keep170frames. Preserve normal speed and complete two-frame pairs.
